First, we substitute $u=7x+3.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=7\,⟹\,\frac{1}{7}\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=7x+3$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $-1$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-4$ | $-\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{1}{(7x+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}\frac{1}{7{u}^{3}}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{1}{(7x+3)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}\frac{1}{7{u}^{3}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{7}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-4}{u}^{-3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-4}{u}^{-3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-2}]}_{a}^{-4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}]}_{a}^{-4} \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-4)^{2}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{16}-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}\cdot (\frac{1}{16}-0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{224}.\end{aligned}
$$
